channels.name: Art for Kids Hub
channels.why: A dad and his kids break every drawing into simple step-by-step shapes so any child feels like a real artist after one video.
channels.note: Draw-along and watercolor/origami lessons, ~5-10 min, near-daily; the whole family model makes it warm and beginner-safe.

channels.name: Draw So Cute
channels.why: Turns everyday objects, animals and food into cute cartoon characters, showing kids how a few lines become an expressive drawing.
channels.note: How-to-draw plus coloring and simple crafts, calm narration, long-form; advertiser-safe.

channels.name: Muffalo Potato
channels.why: Teaches kids to build cartoons entirely out of numbers and letters, quietly reinforcing letter/number recognition through art.
channels.note: Weekly draw-alongs, gentle host, ~5-8 min; clever shape-from-symbols method.

channels.name: Cartooning Club How to Draw
channels.why: Slow, clear cartoon-drawing lessons that show the underlying construction shapes before adding detail, shading and color.
channels.note: Very high cadence (near-daily), pop-culture and original characters; kid-friendly and easy to follow.

channels.name: Mark Crilley
channels.why: A published manga author demystifies faces, figures and realistic drawing with narrated step-by-step technique that builds real skill.
channels.note: Manga/comics and realism, long-form tutorials; skews to older, more patient kids.

channels.name: Circle Line Art School
channels.why: Makes perspective and optical illusions click, teaching kids how 1- and 2-point perspective turns flat lines into 3D rooms and cities.
channels.note: Weekly perspective/technique tutorials, spare narration, long-form; great for spatial thinkers.

channels.name: Watercolor4KIDS
channels.why: Introduces real watercolor technique - wet-on-wet, blending, layering - in short projects designed specifically for young hands.
channels.note: Emily Olson teaches with her daughter using affordable paints; friendly and low-pressure.

channels.name: Draw With Rob (Rob Biddulph)
channels.why: A bestselling children's illustrator leads joyful draw-alongs that convince kids anyone can make a great picture together.
channels.note: #DrawWithRob draw-along series, ~15-20 min, upbeat; excellent for shared parent-child drawing time.

channels.name: Draw with Jazza
channels.why: Explores digital and traditional art through inventive challenges that show kids how professionals experiment, iterate and problem-solve.
channels.note: Digital art, animation and art challenges, long-form; energetic pacing, best for older kids and occasional mild goofiness.

channels.name: Kasey Golden (Kasey The Golden)
channels.why: Playful watercolor and gouache tutorials and tip lists that teach color mixing and technique while celebrating creative experimentation.
channels.note: Watercolor/illustration, long-form, calm and encouraging; some content is supply reviews so curate to the tutorials.

channels.name: Fun2draw (Mei Yu)
channels.why: An award-winning illustrator teaches easy chibi, cartoon and anime drawing that gives kids quick, confidence-building wins.
channels.note: Cute cartoon/anime style, long-form, cheerful; large back catalog of simple characters.

channels.name: Carla Sonheim
channels.why: Encourages imaginative, loose drawing and painting of invented animals, freeing kids from the fear of a 'wrong' way to draw.
channels.note: Creative process and mixed-media lessons incl. a Kids Art Week series; mostly adult-oriented so pick the kid lessons. Handle not fully confirmed.
